Longer than I like to admit. I joined in two thousand and four.
Twenty years in one place. That is rare now.
It is. I started as an analyst, and I spent the first three years just reading contracts.

Then I got a promotion to the corporate desk. That was the turning point, honestly.
Why that one?

Right, so, my story. I joined the company in two thousand and nine, straight out of university, in the smallest office we had. For two years I did nothing but data entry, and I was terrible at it. In two thousand and twelve they offered me an assignment in Mexico for six months. I said yes without thinking, and that was the turning point. I came back speaking Spanish, and suddenly I was the person who handled the whole region. I got my first promotion the following year. Eventually they moved me to head office, and I have been here ever since. Fifteen years, one company. My mother still asks when I am going to get a proper job.

One last thing before you go. For tomorrow morning, we would like each of you to prepare a short career story. Two minutes, no slides, no notes. Tell us three things: where you started, one moment that changed your direction, and where you are now. We are not looking for a CV. We had someone last year who spent the whole two minutes listing job titles, and by the end nobody remembered a single one. Tell us the story instead. Two minutes. Tomorrow, at nine.
